title: "Bass line: Roots on every beat"
subtitle: "For bass, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2

This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Roots on every beat**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

The root of the chord on every beat and nothing else. The plainest line there is, under driving eighths or a strummed song.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock*, *Piano ballad*, *Boom-chick*, *Ska / reggae*, *Acoustic strum*, *Hymn (four parts)*, *Folk carol* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Held roots (the bass voice)

Start with something simpler. The root of every chord, held until the next chord: the bass part of a four-part hymn.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-held.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Held roots (the bass voice)","opts":{"bassFeel":"held"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Roots on 1 and 3

The root on beats 1 and 3, held; one note a bar in 3/4. A chord that changes in between gets its root when it arrives.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-halves.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Roots on every beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A root on every beat, every note the same length. Keep the plucking hand alternating (index, middle) and the fretting finger down for the whole bar. The test is evenness: record yourself and listen for one beat that is louder or later than the others.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}},{"label":"Roots on 1 and 3 (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"halves"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-meter="3/4" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Roots on every beat","opts":{"bassFeel":"roots"}}]'></div>

## How it relates to the other patterns

- **Builds on:** [Held roots (the bass voice)](bass-held.qmd), [Roots on 1 and 3](bass-halves.qmd).
- **Leads to:** [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass-dotted.qmd), [Octaves (disco)](bass-octaves.qmd), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass-polka.qmd), [Chord tones (learning to walk)](bass-arp.qmd), [Boogie-woogie](bass-boogie.qmd), [Boogie-woogie octaves](bass-boogie-oct.qmd), [Chameleon: chromatic pickup](bass-chameleon.qmd): the patterns that use this one as a step.
- **The same idea elsewhere in the band:** [Quarter-note chords](chords-quarters.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Strum: downstrokes on the beat](chords-strum-quarters.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Hi-hat: quarter notes](drums-hhquarters.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Plays with, in straight-eighth rock:** [Strum: down-up eighths](chords-strum-eights.qmd) (comping rhythm), [Rock backbeat](drums-rock.qmd) (drum groove).
- **Other bass lines in the Folk, rock and pop group:** [Root and fifth](bass-alt.qmd), [Root and fifth on every beat](bass-polka.qmd), [3+3+2 (tresillo)](bass-tresillo.qmd), [Root eighths](bass-eighths.qmd), [Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)](bass-dotted.qmd), [Octaves (disco)](bass-octaves.qmd), [Motown: root, fifth, octave](bass-motown.qmd), [12/8 ballad](bass-twelve8.qmd).
